correction: DONE is right: the poll, the spawn per read, the missing cause and the missing backoff are all fixed. The auditor's 'no concrete defects' is wrong. Removing the 30 s poll also removed the only automatic repair for two failure cases, and the replacement triggers do not cover them (see fixDefects). Minor: the historyRecoveryPolicy.ts range should be 142-178; the file ends at 178.
summary: The finding's costs are gone. The forever loop of reconcile plus a 30 s sleep (f1be4abc7 orchestrationRpc.ts:68-80) is replaced by withThreadHistoryRecovery. It reads once when an active subscription opens, then once per thread.session-set event that settles the session, with no timer. A spacing gate (5 min after an open, 30 s after a settle) runs before any SQL. Failures back off from 30 s, doubling to 15 min. The cause is logged at Warning once per failure streak, then at Debug. Stored Codex reads share one pooled read-only app-server per instance that closes after 60 s idle. Clients mark prewarmed and retained idle subscriptions passive, so those read nothing. Optional proposal part 2 (a cheap mtime or updatedAt check before thread/read) was not built. That costs little now that reads are spaced and pooled. A verified side effect: the old poll also repaired turns stuck as running. The new triggers cannot fire in that case, and a settle that lands inside the spacing window is dropped rather than deferred.

evidence.note: withHistoryRecovery now calls withThreadHistoryRecovery with an active/passive mode and a per-connection registry. The Effect.forever loop is gone. It wraps subscribeThread (:610) and subscribeThreadWindow (:643). setThreadHistoryRecovery (:454-459) only flips the mode for this connection.
One forked read on open (only when active, or on a passive-to-active flip). One forked read per stream array that holds a settling thread.session-set event (settlesThreadSession, :46-53). No timer.
Spacing is 5 min after an open and 30 s after a settle. After a failure it is 30 s, doubling up to 15 min.

The spacing gate and the historyReads coalescing set run before resolveThreadShell, getProjectShellById and getBinding. A gated trigger returns Effect.void and nothing is rescheduled. Semaphore(2) bounds admission.

25 s timeout. Warning with Cause.pretty only on the first failure of a streak; repeats go to Debug with threadId, trigger and failures. State is bounded to 1,000 threads (recordHistoryRecovery, :3504-3516).
processHistory returns early on an empty history and uses the bounded getThreadHistoryRepairContext (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:4409) instead of the full getThreadDetailById.

One lazily started read-only app-server per instance, shared by concurrent reads. It closes after 60 s idle (:59) and is retired when the process exits or a transport error occurs. CodexAdapter.ts:2608-2616 uses it for non-live reads. The old per-read readStoredCodexThread (CodexSessionRuntime.ts:1192) is now used only by an integration test.
A subscription sends historyRecovery active only while a view is attached (viewCount > 0). View attach and detach call setThreadHistoryRecovery.

Defect evidence: a live Codex session emits session.state.changed 'ready' only from session/ready, once at startup (CodexSessionRuntime.ts:2261). thread/status/changed idle maps to thread.state.changed, and ingestion turns that into nothing except compaction (ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:1036-1039). If turn.completed is lost, no settling thread.session-set is ever produced.

Defect evidence: the liveness sweep settles a running turn only when no live runtime exists ('lost'). On a live runtime it only reports 'unresponsive' once and never acts. Before, the 30 s poll healed this case through the settlesTurn path (ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:3421-3439, decider.ts:2845-2874).

fixDefects: (1) Lost turn completion on a live runtime is no longer repaired while the thread stays open. Suppose turn.completed is dropped or fails in processInputSafely (ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:3474-3488) while the Codex runtime stays up. The projected turn then stays 'running', and nothing emits a settling thread.session-set: thread/status/changed maps to thread.state.changed, which is ignored, and session/ready is only emitted at startup. So the session-settled trigger never fires. The liveness sweep only reports 'unresponsive' for a live runtime. Repair now waits for an active subscribe at least 5 min after the last read, a manual stop, or a server restart. Before, the 30 s poll repaired it through the settlesTurn and pending-request clearing paths of processHistory, which exist for exactly this case. A dead runtime is now marked 'lost' (error) after about 2 sweeps, instead of being settled as completed from provider history. (2) A trigger that lands inside the spacing window is dropped, not deferred: reconcileThread returns Effect.void at :3524-3526 and nothing reschedules it. A common case is a thread opened at T0 (read) whose next turn settles before T0+30 s, or two turns that settle within 30 s of each other. The final turn never gets an end-of-turn read until the next settle or a reopen 5 min later. (3) Freshness trade-off, by design of the proposal: an open thread advanced by another writer (the Codex app holding the writer lease, CodexAdapter.ts:2597-2598) no longer picks up those turns within 30 s; it waits for a reopen after 5 min. Minor: the 25 s HISTORY_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT also covers waiting for the Semaphore(2) permit, so a large burst of opens could log a timeout as a failure. Not seen in practice.
implementationSketch: 1) Trailing read instead of a dropped trigger. In ProviderRuntimeIngestion.reconcileThread (:3517-3527), when a 'session-settled' trigger is gated by the success spacing (state.failures === 0), keep a per-thread pendingTrailing set. Fork one Effect.sleep(remaining).pipe(Effect.andThen(reconcileThread(threadId, 'session-settled'))) in the layer scope, deduped per thread and dropped when a read runs first. Or do it in withThreadHistoryRecovery so the subscription scope cancels it: make reconcile report 'gated until X' and schedule one delayed fork. Test in ProviderRuntimeIngestion.test.ts with TestClock: open, then settle at +10 s gives one read now and one at +30 s, never more. 2) Repair a lost completion on a live runtime. ProviderCommandReactor.sweepLiveness (ProviderCommandReactor.ts:3364-3400) already visits every thread with a projected running turn and live runtime activity. When classifyThreadLiveness sees a matching live runtime that has been silent for at least one sweep interval (or the adapter session reports no active turn), call an injected requestHistoryRecovery(threadId). That is ProviderRuntimeIngestionService.reconcileThread with a new 'liveness' trigger: settled spacing plus failure backoff, added to HistoryRecoveryTrigger and historyRecoverySpacingMs. Inject it as an optional layer dependency or reactor option so the reactor does not depend on ingestion internals. It costs nothing for idle threads, since only projected-running threads qualify. Test: drop turn.completed in the ingestion harness, run sweepLiveness, and assert thread.history.restore settles the turn and clears pending requests. 3) Optional, product decision: freshness for external writers. While a view is active, poll a cheap updatedAt probe every 60 s (thread/read includeTurns:false on the shared CodexStoredThreadReader, or a rollout file stat). Do the full includeTurns read only when it changed. This also covers proposal part 2.
decisionReason: Fixes 1 and 2 restore the lost safety net without polling idle threads, so they need no decision. Only the optional fix 3 (polling the viewed thread for changes from another writer) is a product trade-off between freshness and background cost.
